ghs.en: Touko was here.

rows.jp: というか、いっつも一等賞じゃないか、こいつ。
rows.en: Come to think of it, wasn’t she always the first one here?

ghs.en: Or should I say, alllways shooting for first place, ain't she.
ghs.assessment: He remarks that she is always the first-place arrival, not that she is continually aspiring or trying to win first place. The English turns an observed result into intention.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She's always first place, isn't she?'

ghs.en: Taichi: "'morning."
Touko: "...(pfuiri)"
Ostracism?
ghs.assessment: The slang asks whether she is ignoring him. 'Ostracism' denotes broader social exclusion and changes the immediate interpersonal act.

rows.en: So it was the silent treatment.

ghs.en: Is this ostracism I see?
ghs.assessment: The repeated slang asks whether she is ignoring him. 'Ostracism' again substitutes a different, broader social process.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wear..."
ghs.assessment: The isolated noun is 'underwear' or 'panties,' setting up the following exchange. 'Wear' is not that noun and removes the joke's concrete object.

ghs.en: Touko: "Be succint."
ghs.assessment: She calls him persistent or tiresome for repeating himself. The English orders him to be concise, changes the speech act, and misspells 'succinct.'

ghs.en: Taichi: "Please buy what I wear?"
ghs.assessment: He explicitly asks her to buy him underwear. The vague paraphrase 'what I wear' suppresses the concrete object that drives the exchange.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Won't you buy me some underwear?'

rows.jp: 「どーして私があなたのパンツを買わないといけないのっ！」
rows.en: “Why do I have to buy your underwear?!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Whyyy would I ever need to buy what you wear?!"
ghs.assessment: She explicitly protests having to buy his underwear. The vague paraphrase removes the repeated noun and weakens the comic escalation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Why do I have to buy your underwear?'

rows.jp: 机をどついて立ちあがる冬子。
rows.en: Touko slammed the desk and stood up.

ghs.en: Touko stands, slamming fists on the desk.

rows.en: “Hot this early in the morning, huh?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "All hott' from morning ain'tcha."
I give her a thumbs up.
Touko: "..."

rows.jp: 冬子は親指をぐっとつかんで、ごきっと横に折った。
rows.en: Touko seized my thumb and wrenched it sideways with a crack.

ghs.en: Youko grabs my thumb tightly, and harshly twists it along with my wrist.
ghs.assessment: She grips his thumb and bends it sideways with a crack. The English turns this into twisting the thumb together with his wrist and loses the specified break-like motion.
ghs.remedy: Say that she bent his thumb sideways with a crack.

highlights.text: twists it along with my wrist

ghs.en: Taichi: "GhyEEEEEEEH!!!"

rows.jp: 「あほーっ、折れたらどうするのだーっ！　自慰もままならないではないかーっ！」
rows.en: “You idiot! What if you’d broken it?! I wouldn’t even be able to masturbate properly!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Morooon, what if you'd broken iiit! I would never manage to console myself agaaain!"
ghs.assessment: He explicitly complains that he would not even be able to masturbate. 'Console myself' euphemizes away the sexual joke and its reason for mentioning the hand.
ghs.remedy: Use an explicit equivalent of 'I wouldn't even be able to masturbate.'

rows.jp: 危うく手首を返したからよかったものの。
rows.en: Good thing I managed to turn my wrist at the last second, though.

ghs.en: Very fortunately, she only barely managed to twist my wrist.
ghs.assessment: He says it was fortunate that he narrowly turned his wrist, which prevented worse injury. The English makes her the actor who barely managed to twist his wrist and reverses the protective causality.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It was a good thing I managed to turn my wrist in time.'

highlights.text: Very fortunately, she only barely managed to twist my wrist.

ghs.en: Touko: "Stay back and do not talk to me."
ghs.assessment: She only tells him not to talk to her. The English adds a command to keep physically away.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Did you watch TV last night?"
Touko: "Stay back and do not talk to me!"
ghs.assessment: The repeated command again concerns speaking only. The English repeats an unsupported instruction to keep physically away.

ghs.en: Taichi: "...mngh."

rows.jp: 話しかけないでと辛口に言われると、話しかけたくなる。
rows.en: Hearing “don’t talk to me” in that cutting voice only made me want to talk to her.

ghs.en: When I'm told in harsh tones not to approach or talk, I end up wanting to get close and talk.
ghs.assessment: Being sharply told not to speak makes him want to speak. The English twice adds physical approach and closeness that are absent from the source.
ghs.remedy: Keep both clauses about talking without adding movement or proximity.

rows.jp: 話しかけると、また、話しかけないでと辛口に言われる。
rows.en: If I did, she’d tell me not to talk to her again in the same cutting voice.

ghs.en: I get close and talk to her, but once more she harshly tells me to stay away and not to talk to her.
ghs.assessment: He talks to her and is again sharply told not to. The English adds both moving close and being ordered to stay away.
ghs.remedy: Keep the exchange about speaking without adding physical-distance commands.

highlights.text: get close and talk to her
stay away and not to talk to her
